title: Blind joint homogenisation of seven SST products (60S-60N, 1982-2025) finds 23 product steps; the products then agree on 0.149 C per decade in 1985-2024 and keep a smaller warming acceleration
abstract: Question: the campaign found steps in NOAA DOISST v2.1 against one reference at a time, at documented dates, but each reference has its own errors. Which product causes each step, and what do satellite-era SST trends look like when all products are homogeneous? Approach: we fitted a joint model X_p(t) = T(t) + c_p + B_p(t) + noise to monthly anomalies of seven products (DOISST v2.1, ESA CCI v3, ERA5, COBE-SST2, ERSSTv5, HadISST1, OISST v2) on one 60S-60N mask of 29,976 points, 1982-2025. A greedy search adds product-specific steps without any date information; null simulations with autocorrelated noise set the threshold. HadSST4.2 and Argo were kept out as independent references. Results: the search finds 23 steps of 0.02-0.07 C (DOISST 5, CCI 5, HadISST1 4, COBE-SST2 3, OISST v2 3, ERSSTv5 2, ERA5 1). Six of 14 steps in products with documented changes fall within 1 month of one (0.87 expected at random), for example DOISST 1985-01, 2005-01, 2016-01 and 2020-06, and CCI 1988-11 and 1991-09. All 8 robustness variants assign the 2020 warm step (+0.04-0.06 C) to DOISST. After homogenisation, the 1985-2024.5 trend at 60S-60N is 0.149-0.150 C per decade in all six full-period products (published 0.108-0.196; variants 0.140-0.150). Against HadSST4.2 and Argo, the spread of product-minus-reference trends falls from 0.024 to 0.0007 and from 0.025 to 0.003 C per decade. In the Merchant et al. (2025) quadratic model, published CCI gives c = 0.027 +/- 0.007 K per decade^2 (they give 0.026); homogenised products give 0.020-0.025 (published 0.017-0.034), and the 2019-23 rate is 0.21-0.22 C per decade (published DOISST 0.29). The acceleration stays but is 15-50% smaller than in published DOISST, ERSSTv5 and CCI. The DOISST 2023/24 jump falls from 0.242 to 0.175 C; homogenised products give 0.175-0.241 C. Limitations: errors that all products share cannot be found, drifts become step staircases, the consensus depends on the product set (mainly ERA5), and some variants also give ERA5 a +0.03 C step in 2020-10.
